To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a new class of dyes that have the potential to be used as acceptor materials in OPVs.
the synthesis and characterization of a new class of unsymmetrical electron acceptors is reported.

we have synthesized new naphthyl derivatives functionalised with electron acceptor units and have investigated their electronic and photophysical properties by optical, computational, and electrochemical techniques and their potential use as electron accepting materials for organic photovolatic applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, characterisation, and theoretical studies of new unsymmetrical naphthyl derivatives containing electron acceptor units.
the design and synthesis of novel electron acceptor materials with different energy levels and distributions.
the design and synthesis of novel electron acceptors, which could be useful for the preparation of organic solar cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the naphthalene moiety can be used as a versatile electron donor in OPV devices.
the naphthyl derivatives are not suitable as electron acceptors in blends with the common donor polymers P3 HT and PCDT BT.

the nature of the substituent at the 2 position of the naphthalene unit plays a crucial role in the packing of the material, and that the nature of this substituent also has an effect on the electronic structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the introduction of a naphthoquinone unit as an electron acceptor in the unsymmetrical diphthalocyanine dyes results in a dye with an HOMO level similar to the one of unsubstituted diphthalocianine and with a LUMO level shifted to lower energy.

we have designed a series of dyes containing a common naphthyl donor connected to a series of acceptors, which have been characterised by a variety of techniques and the results have been discussed in detail.
the introduction of electron acceptor units into the naphthyl core of the molecule allows for a tuning of the LUMOs energy levels and their distribution, and thus the design of new dyes for OPVs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LUMO level of the dyes is not the only factor that controls charge separation and that the distribution of the LUMOs through the molecule is also important.
the electron acceptor moietyl unit has a major influence on the optical and electronic properties of the molecule.
the nature and position of the electron acceptor strongly influence the electronic properties of the dye and the photophysical properties of the blends.
